Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1.85 billion for the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54 percent from a year earlier, and earnings per share of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16 [D1]. Net income of 397 million rose 107.85 percent from a year earlier and earnings per share rose 63.95 percent, so profit grew faster than sales [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87 percent and net margin was 21.51 percent, and the earnings coverage attributed the margin expansion to stronger revenue and disciplined cost management [D2]. Communications Solutions Group revenue was 1,345 million, up 43.09 percent, and its operating income was 458 million, up 86.18 percent, so the segment turned sales growth into profit growth at roughly double the rate [D1]. Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was 501 million, up 21.6 percent, and its operating income was 155 million, up 68.48 percent [D1]. The release described a second consecutive record quarter, with orders rising sharply from a year earlier on demand for testing linked to AI infrastructure [D1]. The company guided fourth fiscal quarter revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion, which the release put at year-over-year growth of approximately 37 percent at the midpoint, and non-GAAP earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of 172 million [D1].

Shares rose in pre-market trading after the results, which the coverage attributed to earnings and revenue comfortably exceeding Wall Street expectations [D2]. The same report said orders provided one of the strongest signals from the quarter, with demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure a major contributor to the increase [D2]. That report also said commercial communications revenue jumped, that the wireline business benefited substantially from accelerating AI data centre investment, and that wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history [D2]. The call coverage recorded management saying wireline delivered record orders that more than doubled year over year, and that software and services both grew double digits [D3]. The fourth-quarter guidance came in well above the analyst consensus for both revenue and earnings per share, which the coverage read as evidence that strong demand could continue beyond the latest quarter [D2].

On the call, analysts probed the sustainability of the order level and whether supply constraints were capping the guidance, and management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue [D3]. Management said demand is not the limiter and that supply will govern its ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters, and called the supply situation likely to be nonlinear [D3]. The call summary said management guided fourth-quarter orders to be slightly up from the third quarter in line with seasonality, supported by a rolling funnel that stands at an all-time high [D4]. That summary said the 6G opportunity is projected to be larger than the 5G cycle, with customers moving from exploratory research into funded development programs, and that integration of recent acquisitions was completed a quarter ahead of schedule [D4]. Management cautioned that one-time tariff impacts lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. The company said most of the targeted cost synergies from its acquisitions are expected to be realized on a run-rate basis by the end of the fiscal year [D3].

An opinion piece linked from the call coverage argues that the artificial intelligence growth is strong but that the valuation leaves little room for error, which is its writer's argument [D3]. The price target piece reports that the shares gained over the prior four weeks and that the mean of the analysts' short-term targets implies a potential upside from the recent price, and argues that upward revisions to the earnings estimate and a top-ranked score strengthen the case for the shares, which is its argument [D5]. The same piece argues that analyst price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide, because firms setting them often have business incentives to drum up interest in the shares, which is its argument [D5]. The company said its management team will participate in investor conferences with fireside chats in the coming weeks, with live webcasts and replays accessible through its investor relations site [D6].
